context: The source string s is bag (length 3), and the target string t is pack (length 4). These inputs differ from other examples in the text. Each operation inserts, deletes, or replaces one character at a cost of 1.

The state dp[i, j] is the minimum number of edits needed to turn the first i characters of s (the source prefix) into the first j characters of t (the target prefix). The table has 4 rows and 5 columns. Rows i = 0 through 3 correspond to the empty string, b, ba, and bag. Columns j = 0 through 4 correspond to the empty string, p, pa, pac, and pack.
description: Start with a 4×5 table of zeros. The value dp[0, 0] is already the correct boundary value of 0 for converting the empty string to itself. Initialize the positive-length entries of the first row to dp[0, j] = j, since inserting j characters into the empty string gives the target prefix. Initialize those of the first column to dp[i, 0] = i, since deleting i characters from the source prefix gives the empty string. Compute the 12 interior cells from top to bottom, moving left to right in each row.

To compute dp[i, j], compare the last character of the source prefix, s[i - 1], with the last character of the target prefix, t[j - 1]. If they match, no new edit is needed: copy the upper-left value dp[i - 1, j - 1] without adding 1. If they differ, take the minimum of the value on the left, dp[i, j - 1] (insertion), the value above, dp[i - 1, j] (deletion), and the upper-left value, dp[i - 1, j - 1] (replacement), then add 1. Each step includes a complete state table with a distinct name. Every cell gives its value and a status: “valid boundary,” “computed,” or “initial value, not yet computed.” Step 15 marks the lower-right cell as the “return value.” Row and column headers give i or j and the corresponding prefix, so you can look up a cell by coordinates or prefixes.

The other 19 cells hold initial values yet to be computed, including the positive-length boundaries in the first row and first column.

frames.announcement: Initialize the first row to the costs of inserting into the empty string, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], and the first column to the costs of deleting down to the empty string, [0, 1, 2, 3].
frames.explanation: Keep dp[0, 0] = 0 for converting the empty string to itself. Set the first row from dp[0, 0] through dp[0, 4] to [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]. Starting from the empty string, each target prefix (the empty string, p, pa, pac, or pack) requires j insertions, one for each character. For the empty string to pack, dp[0, 4] = 4. Set the first column from dp[0, 0] through dp[3, 0] to [0, 1, 2, 3]. Each source prefix (the empty string, b, ba, or bag) requires i deletions to reach the empty string. For bag to the empty string, dp[3, 0] = 3. The 12 zeros in rows 1 through 3 and columns 1 through 4 are still initial values yet to be computed.
frames.key_state: The empty-string boundaries are set. The first row is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] (dp[0, 4] = 4), and the first column is [0, 1, 2, 3] (dp[3, 0] = 3).

frames.title: Initialize the empty-string boundaries in the first row and column

frames.announcement: Compute dp[1, 1] (b to p). The final characters b and p differ. Add 1 to the smallest of the three values, 0, to get 1.
frames.explanation: At i = 1, j = 1, compute dp[1, 1] for converting the source prefix b to the target prefix p. The final characters b and p differ. Compare the cell to the left, dp[1, 0] = 1, the cell above, dp[0, 1] = 1, and the upper-left cell, dp[0, 0] = 0. Add 1 to the minimum value 0 and write dp[1, 1] = 1. This edit replaces b with p.
frames.key_state: dp[1, 1] (source prefix b to target prefix p): the final characters b and p differ. min(left 1, above 1, upper left 0) + 1 = 1.

frames.key_state: dp[1, 2] (source prefix b to target prefix pa): the final characters b and a differ. min(left 1, above 2, upper left 1) + 1 = 2.

frames.key_state: dp[1, 3] (source prefix b to target prefix pac): the final characters b and c differ. min(left 2, above 3, upper left 2) + 1 = 3.

This match requires no new edit. Copy the upper-left result dp[1, 1] = 1 for b to p without adding 1, and write dp[2, 2] = 1.

Compare the cell to the left, dp[2, 2] = 1, the cell above, dp[1, 3] = 3, and the upper-left cell, dp[1, 2] = 2. Add 1 to the minimum value 1 on the left and write dp[2, 3] = 2. This inserts c after the 1 edit that turns ba into pa.
